references.text: Here Nicodemus is mentioned as coming to Jesus at night, an event that directly prepares for his later intervention in John 7:50 where he reminds them that he has already come to Jesus before.
Nicodemus is mentioned again together with Joseph of Arimathea, and here it is confirmed that he had already come to Jesus earlier, which is the central identification in John 7:50.

The context for John 7:50 is the debate between the religious leaders and Nicodemus, who defends Jesus by pointing out that the law requires a hearing before judgment, linking this to his role as one of those who have come to Jesus.

The text describes that many of the leaders, including Nicodemus, believed in Jesus but did not confess it publicly because of fear of the religious leaders, which explains his cautious intervention in John 7:50.
